reading.body:
Otter.ai makes money by selling access to meeting transcripts and summaries to users and to external AI tools like ChatGPT and Claude via its MCP Server, which means the company sits between humans, their meetings, and the AI systems that will analyze them.

The core product captures meeting audio through multiple channels and converts it to text and structured summaries in real time. This positions Otter.ai as infrastructure for the emerging workflow where meetings generate training data, analysis, and follow-up actions without manual transcription. The MCP Server integration is the strategic move: by letting other AI systems query meeting content directly, Otter.ai becomes a data broker between enterprises and the AI stack.

For compute scaling, this matters because meeting data is becoming an input to AI systems at scale. If enterprise workflows increasingly feed meeting transcripts into AI analysis and decision-making, demand for transcription infrastructure grows with AI adoption, not separately from it. The data does not show Otter.ai's power consumption, infrastructure footprint, or server locations, so the company's direct claims on the grid remain opaque. It also does not show how much meeting data Otter.ai retains, how it trains models on that data, or what consent frameworks govern access by external AI systems, all of which determine whether transcription is a neutral pipe or a data collection play.

profile_text.body:
Otter.ai is a software company that provides AI-powered meeting transcription and note-taking tools. Its core product, the Otter AI Meeting Agent, offers real-time transcription, live chat during meetings, automated summaries, and action item extraction. The company describes itself as recognized by the Wall Street Journal as a must-try AI tool, and its OtterPilot product is presented as an AI meeting assistant. Users can capture meetings automatically via a bot, through a desktop or Chrome recorder, or on mobile, and a connected Otter AI Chat feature searches across meetings and linked applications to answer questions and help generate follow-ups, reports, and other content.

Otter.ai also offers an MCP Server that allows external AI tools, including ChatGPT and Claude, to access meeting content for analysis and workflow integration. The company's product is categorized in the notes, knowledge, and meetings space, with consent noted as a relevant consideration given its transcription functionality. No litigation or SEC filings are reflected in the held facts.
